PagerBot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT: routing error rate spike detected in dedicated pools (region-us-west) — alert_id=INC-2026-4372
Sam (oncall): seeing it, paging Lee and Ash. I’m pulling graphs
Sam (oncall): topline — 5xx rate from router -> dedicated pools jumped 9% at 09:12 UTC, latency doubled for a subset of customers
Lee (infra): I’m on it, checking autoscaler signals and pool heartbeats
Ash (runtime): also checking fallback policy logs, could be wrong variant routing when pool reports capacity 0
Nina (sre): tagging P0, notify customer-facing if >15m impact. Sam, please confirm customer impact window
Sam (oncall): initial scope: ~30 customers traffic routed to dedicated pool groups in us-west1. Error mix: 503 gateway and 502 from backends. CPU/GPU utilization on hosts looks low. weird.
Lee (infra): pulling router metrics: looks like the dedicated router decided nodes were unhealthy because metric "gpu_ready_count" dipped to 0 for pool d-pool-usw-3 at 09:11:52. But exporter shows GPUs present.
Lee (infra): command I ran:
```
kubectl -n redwood-system get pods -l pool=d-pool-usw-3 -o wide
# pods show Running (3/3) with GPUs attached
```
Sam (oncall): so router misread the signal. Could be prometheus exporter flapping or a label mismatch
Ash (runtime): checking router logs for the fallback decision:
```
2026-03-15T09:11:52Z router decision: pool=d-pool-usw-3 capacity_signal=0 -> fallback_action=route-other-region
2026-03-15T09:11:53Z router -> routed 240 req/s to eu-west-1 variant: v1-quant
```
Ash (runtime): note: fallback routed to eu-west-1 variant v1-quant which is not compatible with some pinned model variants customers use — that could explain blackholed requests (model mismatch -> 502)
Lee (infra): checking prometheus scrape logs — looks like the metrics exporter dropped a label (node_id) for ~30s due to a recent sidecar restart after today's deploy. exporter logs: "WARN: missing gpu_ready_count label for node_id"
Nina (sre): timeline looks like exporter restart at 09:11:40, router decision at 09:11:52, spike at 09:12:00. Impact start ~09:12.
Sam (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) Temporarily disable cross-region fallback for dedicated pools (set policy->no-fallback) 2) Force router to re-evaluate pool health 3) Restart exporter sidecar on affected nodes 4) Notify customers and track errors.
Lee (infra): applying temporary policy via CI flag now.
Ash (runtime): Sam — run the command to set policy? I can if you want.
Sam (oncall): I’ll run it.
Sam (oncall): `POST /admin/policies/dedicated-routing` payload: `{ "pool_match": "d-pool-usw-*", "fallback": "disabled", "reason": "emergency: misread gpu_ready_count causing cross-region fallback" }`
PagerBot: Policy change event: policy_id=pol-9223 applied by Sam at 09:15:02 UTC — fallback disabled for pools matching d-pool-usw-*
Lee (infra): forcing router refresh: `curl -XPOST http://router-admin.local/refresh-pools?pool=d-pool-usw-3` -> 200 OK
Ash (runtime): restarted sidecar on node-7 and node-9 (where exporter showed missing labels). restart logs:
```
systemctl restart redwood-exporter && journalctl -u redwood-exporter -n 50
# exporter now reporting gpu_ready_count=4
```
Sam (oncall): I'm seeing requests reflow back to us-west within 90s. Error rate decreasing.
Nina (sre): customer-impact check: SLO breach window 09:12–09:17 UTC for subset of users. Estimated affected qps: 280 at peak.
Lee (infra): double-checking autoscaler: there was a soft scale-down in progress at 09:10 due to low sustained utilization; combined with exporter flapping the router assumed 0 capacity. autoscaler didn't cause blackhole but increased sensitivity. logging snippet:
```
2026-03-15T09:10:02 autoscaler: scale_down_decision pool=d-pool-usw-3 desired_replicas=2 -> 1 (cooldown)
```
Ash (runtime): root cause narrative draft: exporter sidecar restarted (deploy ripple), Prometheus scrape missed gpu_ready_count labels for ~30s, router health evaluation saw capacity 0 -> fallback triggered to eu-west variant which is incompatible for pinned customers -> blackholed traffic and 502/503 spikes. Secondary factor: autoscaler cooldown meant fewer replicas so sensitivity higher.
Sam (oncall): mitigation complete? Error rate back to baseline and latency improving. I’m keeping fallback disabled until we confirm exporter stable for 10m.
Nina (sre): Ops follow-ups: - revert emergency policy after postmortem - instrument exporter restart alerts - add router debounce on capacity signal to avoid single-scrape flaps - update runbook for oncall handoffs.
Lee (infra): adding prometheus alert: alert name: ExporterLabelDrop, expr: absent(gpu_ready_count{node_id=~".*"}) for 15s -> severity=page
Ash (runtime): I'll schedule a patch to router logic: require 2 consecutive missing scrapes before treating pool as zero-capacity.
Sam (oncall): handing off to Lee for next 4hr window — watch exporter alerts and policy pol-9223. If stable after 30m, I will revert policy.
Lee (infra): ack — taking handoff. leaving notes: monitor error-rate, router-decision logs, export logs on node-7/9.
Sam (oncall): customer comms: Support, please inform impacted customers A/B with timestamps and mitigation steps. Nina, can you trigger the customer incident template?
Nina (sre): yes, sending template now. ETA mail 09:28.
PagerBot: Incident INC-2026-4372 status=mitigated by Sam at 09:18:15 UTC — followups assigned: postmortem (Ash), alert tuning (Lee), customer comms (Nina).
Sam (oncall): final notes: timeframe 09:12–09:17 UTC, root cause exporter sidecar label drop + router sensitivity, mitigation: emergency policy disable + exporter restart, long-term: debounce + alerting + runbook. handing off.
Lee (infra): copied. closing thread for oncall handoff.
